name: glossary-academic
description: Glossary-style: term definition stored first, then three question types per term — direct definition, surrounding concept, superseding term.

glossary: Self-attention: a mechanism where each token in a sequence computes a weighted representation of all other tokens, with weights from query-key dot products scaled by sqrt(d_k). Core building block of Transformer models.
RNN: a recurrent architecture processing tokens sequentially while maintaining a hidden state; suffers from vanishing gradients on long sequences.
Mamba: a state-space-model architecture with selective scan giving linear-time sequence modeling, positioned as an alternative to Transformers.
cases.question: What is self-attention?
cases.expected_answer: Each token computes a weighted representation of all other tokens using scaled query-key dot products; the core Transformer mechanism.

glossary: Self-attention: a mechanism where each token in a sequence computes a weighted representation of all other tokens, with weights from query-key dot products scaled by sqrt(d_k). Core building block of Transformer models.
Transformer: an architecture built entirely on self-attention, removing recurrence and enabling full parallelization during training.
KV cache: storing key/value tensors of past tokens so autoregressive decoding avoids recomputation.
cases.question: Why do Transformers parallelize training better than RNNs?
reasoning_chain: self-attention sees all tokens at once
cases.expected_answer: Because self-attention lets every token attend to every other token in one pass, removing the sequential recurrence RNNs require.

glossary: RNN: a recurrent architecture processing tokens sequentially while maintaining a hidden state; suffers from vanishing gradients on long sequences.
LSTM: an RNN variant with gating cells that mitigates vanishing gradients for longer dependencies.
Transformer: an architecture built entirely on self-attention, removing recurrence; largely replaced LSTM/RNN models in NLP after 2017.
cases.question: What replaced LSTMs as the dominant NLP architecture?
cases.expected_answer: The Transformer — self-attention based, replaced recurrent architectures after 2017.

glossary: MapReduce: a distributed batch-processing framework where jobs are expressed as map and reduce phases over shuffled intermediate data; batch-oriented.
Spark: an in-memory distributed computation engine supporting iterative and interactive workloads with RDDs/DataFrames; generally superseded MapReduce for analytics workloads.
HDFS: the Hadoop distributed filesystem storing replicated blocks across cluster nodes.
cases.question: What is MapReduce's main limitation that led to its decline for analytics?
reasoning_chain: Spark keeps data in memory, handles iteration
cases.expected_answer: It writes intermediate results to disk between batch phases, making iterative and interactive analytics slow — Spark's in-memory model superseded it.

glossary: pgvector: a PostgreSQL extension adding a vector column type with exact and approximate (HNSW, IVFFlat) nearest-neighbor search.
HNSW: hierarchical navigable small world graphs — an approximate nearest-neighbor index offering logarithmic search with high recall.
IVFFlat: an inverted-file approximate index clustering vectors into lists and searching the closest lists only.
